content.text:
droid-monkey attacked this Android app with a real-world fault and it failed. Fix the root cause.

## What happened
Attack `process_death` (process_death): Fill the screen's form, let Android kill the app in the background, then come back to it.
Steps: [{"fill": true}, {"fault": "kill_in_background"}, {"fault": "relaunch"}, {"settle": 6}]
Result: lost_state: 6 of 6 filled fields changed or emptied
Fields lost (before -> after): {'field_name': ['Ravi Kumar', ''], 'field_email': ['ravi@example.com', ''], 'field_phone': ['9876543210', ''], 'field_address': ['12 MG Road', ''], 'field_city': ['Bengaluru', ''], 'field_pincode': ['560001', '']}

## Diagnosis
Root cause: The checkout form's six fields are plain `mutableStateOf` properties on `CheckoutViewModel` (CheckoutViewModel.kt:17-22), and the ViewModel is constructed with no `SavedStateHandle`. The navigation route survives process death because `MainActivity` stores it with `rememberSaveable` (MainActivity.kt:62), so the app restores to the Checkout screen. But the ViewModel is recreated empty, and the `CheckoutScreen` fields bind to its empty properties (CheckoutScreen.kt:34, 67-72). Process death therefore wipes the typed data while the screen itself comes back.
Fix approach: Take a `SavedStateHandle` as the first constructor argument and back each field with it, e.g. `val name get() = handle.getStateFlow(...)` or a delegate that reads and writes `handle["field_name"]`, so values go into the saved-instance bundle and survive process death. Keep the `scope` parameter optional after the handle so the default `viewModel()` factory can supply it. The screen code can stay as it is, since it still reads and writes the same properties.
Evidence: app/src/main/java/com/shubhasai/monkeymart/ui/CheckoutViewModel.kt:14 - ViewModel takes only an optional CoroutineScope; no SavedStateHandle; app/src/main/java/com/shubhasai/monkeymart/ui/CheckoutViewModel.kt:17-22 - the six form fields are plain mutableStateOf(""), so they are not saved and are lost when the process dies; app/src/main/java/com/shubhasai/monkeymart/ui/CheckoutViewModel.kt:32 - isComplete is derived from those unsaved fields, so the Place order button comes back disabled; app/src/main/java/com/shubhasai/monkeymart/ui/CheckoutScreen.kt:34 - vm defaults to viewModel(), which is recreated empty after process death; app/src/main/java/com/shubhasai/monkeymart/ui/CheckoutScreen.kt:67-72 - each OutlinedTextField binds to vm.name...vm.pincode, so the screen shows the empty values after restore; app/src/main/java/com/shubhasai/monkeymart/MainActivity.kt:62 - the route is kept with rememberSaveable, so the user returns to Checkout but the form state behind it is gone

## Files to change
- app/src/main/java/com/shubhasai/monkeymart/ui/CheckoutViewModel.kt

## Regression test
Add a JVM unit test `CheckoutViewModelStateTest` in src/test. It constructs `CheckoutViewModel(SavedStateHandle())`, sets `name = "Ravi Kumar"` and `pincode = "560001"`, then asserts that `handle.get<String>("field_name")` and `handle.get<String>("field_pincode")` hold those values. Before the fix this fails because the handle does not exist as a constructor parameter and the values stay in plain state. After the fix it passes. Optionally, add a second assertion that a new VM built from the same handle contents reports `isComplete == true`.

## Rules
- Fix the root cause in the files above with the idiomatic Android approach. Keep the change small and focused.
- Add exactly one regression test file under app/src/test (JVM unit test, preferred) or app/src/androidTest
  (instrumented), using only test libraries the project already has (see app/build.gradle.kts). It must fail on
  the old code and pass on the fixed code.
- Do not change build files or add dependencies. Do not touch unrelated code. Do not commit.
- Before you finish, call the compile tool on your test ('unit' or 'instrumented') and fix every error it reports.
- When done, reply with one short paragraph: what you changed and the test class name.

package com.shubhasai.monkeymart.ui

import androidx.lifecycle.SavedStateHandle
import org.junit.Assert.assertEquals
import org.junit.Assert.assertFalse
import org.junit.Assert.assertTrue
import org.junit.Test

class CheckoutViewModelStateTest {

    @Test
    fun formFields_areWrittenToSavedStateHandle() {
        val handle = SavedStateHandle()
        val vm = CheckoutViewModel(handle)

        vm.name = "Ravi Kumar"
        vm.pincode = "560001"

        assertEquals("Ravi Kumar", handle.get<String>("field_name"))
        assertEquals("560001", handle.get<String>("field_pincode"))
    }

    @Test
    fun newViewModelFromSameHandle_restoresFormState() {
        val handle = SavedStateHandle()
        val first = CheckoutViewModel(handle)
        first.name = "Ravi Kumar"
        first.email = "ravi@example.com"
        first.phone = "9876543210"
        first.address = "12 MG Road"
        first.city = "Bengaluru"
        assertFalse(first.isComplete)
        first.pincode = "560001"

        val restored = CheckoutViewModel(handle)

        assertEquals("Ravi Kumar", restored.name)
        assertTrue(restored.isComplete)
    }
}

content.text: I changed `CheckoutViewModel` to take a `SavedStateHandle` as its first constructor argument, with `scope` now optional after it. Each of the six form fields reads from and writes through to the handle under `field_name`, `field_email`, and so on. I added `@JvmOverloads` so a handle-only constructor exists, which the default `viewModel()` factory needs in order to inject the handle. The unit test source set compiles, but I haven't run the tests or the attack. The new regression test is `CheckoutViewModelStateTest`: it checks that the handle holds the values after they're set, and that a new view model built from the same handle reports `isComplete == true`. I also updated the one constructor call in the existing `CheckoutViewModelTest` to pass `SavedStateHandle()`, since the signature changed.
